tasks.output: {"needs":[{"challengeId":"C001-CH1","triage":"research","triageReason":"Open technical question about unsupervised anomaly detection methods for industrial protocols where labelled attack data does not exist.","restatement":{"text":"Detect unusual behaviour on Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP networks without labelled attack examples (C001-CH1). The company has terabytes of normal traffic archives from three years of client deployments but zero confirmed malicious traffic examples, making supervised classifiers unusable. Previous attempts to train on public ICS datasets produced unacceptable false positive rates in real deployments because models cannot capture site-specific Modbus polling patterns and register usage (C001/blog/2024-05-20). The goal is a method that learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises flags when behaviour drifts from that baseline, operable on-device without degrading packet forwarding latency, and explainable to plant managers in plain language.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1","C001/blog/2024-05-20"]},"searchTerms":["anomaly detection","unsupervised learning","industrial control systems","Modbus TCP","BACnet/IP","network traffic baseline","one-class classification","drift detection","on-device inference"],"assets":[{"text":"Several terabytes of network traffic captures from consenting clients collected over three years.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]},{"text":"Hardware bench with physical NetGuard-OT appliances capable of running inference.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]},{"text":"One engineer with six months of self-directed reading on anomaly detection.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]},{"text":"Existing firmware codebase for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP protocol parsing in C and Rust.","sourceIds":["C001","C001/job/2024-02-05"]},{"text":"Can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to collaborative project.","sourceIds":["C001"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Public ICS datasets do not capture site-specific network behaviour and produced unacceptable false positive rates in real deployments.","sourceIds":["C001/blog/2024-05-20"]},{"text":"Method must run on-device without affecting packet forwarding latency.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]},{"text":"Solution must be explainable to plant managers in plain language for client acceptance.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]},{"text":"Clients have never been breached (or do not know it) so zero examples of confirmed attacks exist.","sourceIds":["C001-CH1"]}]},{"challengeId":"C001-CH2","triage":"engineering-service","triageReason":"A secure firmware update mechanism must be designed and integrated; the core challenge is practical over-the-air delivery with interrupted transfer tolerance, not a novel research question.","restatement":{"text":"Design a secure over-the-air firmware update process for network appliances deployed at remote unmanned sites with poor cellular connectivity (C001-CH2). The company has prototyped three approaches, each with documented failure modes: plain HTTPS with signature verification failed on-device key storage security, dual-partition rollback failed when GPRS dropped mid-transfer leaving the bootloader unable to recover remotely, and download manager with resume support exceeded flash budget on older hardware variants. The solution must tolerate interrupted transfers, work on all four current and legacy hardware variants without retrofitting, introduce no new remote code execution path, and integrate with the existing Embedded Linux firmware architecture.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Three prototyped approaches with documented failure modes and threat model draft.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]},{"text":"Four hardware variants currently shipping, including older boards still under long-term support.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Existing Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build) firmware infrastructure.","sourceIds":["C001"]},{"text":"GPRS and LTE-M cellular backhaul already deployed for remote monitoring.","sourceIds":["C001"]},{"text":"Can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to collaborative project.","sourceIds":["C001"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Must not require hardware retrofitting to older variants.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]},{"text":"GPRS links are unreliable and drop mid-transfer; bootloader must handle this without needing remote intervention at unmanned sites.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]},{"text":"Flash budget on older hardware limits code size; previous resume support approach exceeded this limit.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]},{"text":"On-device key storage on current hardware is not sufficient; previous approach using extracted signing key is unacceptable.","sourceIds":["C001-CH2"]}]},{"challengeId":"C001-CH3","triage":"not-research","triageReason":"This is a methodology and reporting framework problem tied to financial valuation and client negotiation, not a technical or scientific research question.","restatement":{"text":"Develop a repeatable methodology for quantifying financial risk in euros from specific vulnerabilities in industrial control networks for client contract negotiations (C001-CH3). Four clients—three in Serbia and one in Bosnia—have requested risk quantification in SecAudit reports to justify remediation budgets to their boards. The company understands the drivers (production downtime costs, regulatory fines under Serbian energy law, emergency response costs) but lacks a calculation method that survives procurement officer scrutiny and can be applied consistently across different client types (utilities versus manufacturers).","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Records of vulnerabilities identified in SecAudit engagements across multiple client types.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Approximate knowledge of production downtime costs for water utilities and electricity distributors.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Access to published incident cost studies from Western Europe.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Existing audit team experienced with on-site vulnerability discovery.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Published frameworks reviewed are either too abstract or built for IT environments where data breach costs dominate, not production downtime.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Must be documentable and defensible when scrutinised by procurement officers and finance teams.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Must work with existing audit team without hiring a financial analyst.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]},{"text":"Must apply consistently across different client types: utilities and discrete manufacturers.","sourceIds":["C001-CH3"]}]},{"challengeId":"C001-CH4","triage":"engineering-service","triageReason":"A test generation and automation system must be built or integrated; the problem is tooling efficiency and test case maintenance, not a novel research question.","restatement":{"text":"Improve regression test automation to reduce manual effort and increase coverage for firmware releases across four hardware variants with monthly release cycles (C001-CH4). The QA team manually maintains 1,400 test cases in a Python test suite running on physical hardware bench, consuming 35% of total engineering time per cycle and still missing bugs because test cases become out of date. The company previously tried generating tests from internal protocol specifications but the tooling was brittle. The goal is a skeleton test generation system that allows a junior engineer to complete a feature's test cases in one hour instead of one day, integrated with the existing Python test runner and physical hardware bench.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Existing Python-based test runner for hardware-in-the-loop regression testing.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Physical hardware bench with four NetGuard-OT boards and PLC simulators.","sourceIds":["C001/job/2024-03-12"]},{"text":"1,400 existing test cases documenting regression patterns since 2015.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Internal protocol specifications for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP.","sourceIds":["C001"]},{"text":"Monthly release cycle and four hardware variants providing test scope.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Solution must fit inside existing Python-based test runner.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Hardware bench is permanent; solution must not replace physical testing.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Previous test generation tooling built from internal specifications was brittle and abandoned.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Three bugs shipped in past year that regression suite should have caught but did not due to out-of-date test cases.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]},{"text":"Monthly release cycle must be maintained; automation timeline is constrained by this schedule.","sourceIds":["C001-CH4"]}]}]}

{"needs":[{"challengeId":"C005-CH1","triage":"research","triageReason":"The problem requires discovery of power-optimization opportunities in the full embedded system stack that firmware tuning alone has not found; this is an open technical investigation into system-level power dynamics.","restatement":{"text":"The KL-Patch 72 ECG recorder consumes 18 mAh per day when Bluetooth is active (advertised, streaming, or syncing events), and must reduce that by at least 35% to support active patients during the full 72-hour wear period while maintaining sampling rate at 250 Hz or above to preserve clinical signal validity (C005-CH1). The device runs FreeRTOS on a Nordic nRF52840 and uses a 54 mAh lithium cell; firmware tuning of BLE advertising intervals, transition to BLE 5.0 long-range PHY, and MCU variant changes have reached diminishing returns (C005-CH1, C005/job/2024-02-05).","sourceIds":["C005-CH1","C005/job/2024-02-05"]},"searchTerms":["low-power embedded systems","duty cycling radio communication","ARM Cortex-M power optimization","Bluetooth Low Energy power consumption","ADC sampling modes DMA transfers","real-time task scheduling energy efficiency","wearable device battery life","current profiling instrumentation"],"assets":[{"text":"Instrumented reference hardware in the lab with a Keysight N6705C power analyzer capable of measuring full current profiles (C005-CH1, C005/job/2024-02-05).","sourceIds":["C005-CH1","C005/job/2024-02-05"]},{"text":"A lab equipped for electronics prototyping, signal acquisition testing, and device-level EMC pre-compliance testing, with twelve people across hardware, firmware, and algorithm development (C005).","sourceIds":["C005"]},{"text":"Firmware team of five engineers running FreeRTOS on Nordic nRF52840 with existing expertise in BLE duty cycling, advertising intervals, and PHY selection (C005/job/2024-02-05).","sourceIds":["C005/job/2024-02-05"]},{"text":"Field deployment of approximately 2,200 KL-Patch 72 devices per month, providing real-world current profiles and behaviour data from active patients (C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Sampling rate cannot drop below 250 Hz or the clinical validity of the ECG signal is compromised (C005-CH1, C005/job/2024-02-05).","sourceIds":["C005-CH1","C005/job/2024-02-05"]},{"text":"The reduction target is a hard constraint: active current draw must drop by at least 35% (C005-CH1).","sourceIds":["C005-CH1"]},{"text":"Firmware-only changes have been exhausted; the company is now looking beyond the software stack for remaining headroom (C005-CH1).","sourceIds":["C005-CH1"]},{"text":"The company is projecting growth to 4,000 devices per month by Q2 next year and intends to grow the device fleet to 6,000 active patches per month over the following two years (C005, C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005","C005-CH2"]}]},{"challengeId":"C005-CH2","triage":"research","triageReason":"The challenge requires developing a novel lossless compression algorithm specialized to ECG signal structure (quasi-periodicity, baseline wander, wearable electrode noise); this is a signal processing research problem where regulatory constraints (lossless requirement) preclude standard lossy methods.","restatement":{"text":"Kardiolink generates approximately 2 TB of raw three-channel ECG signal per month from 2,200 deployed KL-Patch 72 devices (900 MB per device over 72 hours at 250 Hz sampling, 16-bit samples), and current lossless compression achieves only 3:1 ratio, leaving cloud storage costs at €7,400 per month; the company projects these costs will more than double when device deployment reaches 4,000 units monthly, but cannot adopt lossy compression because the regulatory submission under MDR is built on lossless guarantees requiring a new clinical validation study to change (C005-CH2). A lossless algorithm that exploits ECG-specific signal properties — quasi-periodic structure, baseline wander, wearable electrode noise characteristics — is needed to reduce bandwidth and storage cost while maintaining regulatory compliance (C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2"]},"searchTerms":["lossless signal compression","quasi-periodic time series","ECG feature extraction","wearable biosignal processing","baseline wander removal","entropy coding algorithms","redundancy reduction cardiac signals","dictionary-based compression","context modeling biomedical data"],"assets":[{"text":"Labelled dataset of approximately 140,000 30-minute ECG segments collected from field devices, available for algorithm development and benchmarking under NDA (C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2"]},{"text":"Current deployed fleet generating 2 TB raw signal per month in a production environment with 2,200 devices and growing (C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2"]},{"text":"Team of engineers with expertise in Python and MATLAB for signal processing algorithm prototyping (C005).","sourceIds":["C005"]},{"text":"Existing modified SZ algorithm lossless compression pipeline currently achieving 3:1 ratio (C005).","sourceIds":["C005"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"The algorithm must remain lossless; lossy compression is not permitted because the regulatory submission under MDR is built on lossless guarantees and changing to lossy would require a new clinical validation study and amendments to the technical file (C005-CH2).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2"]},{"text":"The company is under cost pressure: cloud storage costs are already a significant operating expense and threaten profitability at the projected 4,000 device per month scale (C005-CH2, C005).","sourceIds":["C005-CH2","C005"]},{"text":"Kardiolink plans to bring cloud infrastructure costs back in line with 2022 levels while growing the device fleet to 6,000 active patches per month (C005).","sourceIds":["C005"]},{"text":"The company is monitoring industry conversations about archiving processed feature vectors rather than raw signals for older recordings but has not yet adopted that approach because of regulatory uncertainty (C005/blog/2023-11-14).","sourceIds":["C005/blog/2023-11-14"]}]},{"challengeId":"C005-CH3","triage":"not-research","triageReason":"This is regulatory documentation and compliance work under EU MDR; while it requires expertise, it is not a technical or scientific research question and cannot be solved by a research group.","restatement":{"text":"","sourceIds":[]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Two quality engineers on staff competent in the existing manufacturing QMS but without prior MDR submission experience at the technical file level (C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005-CH3"]},{"text":"IEC 62304-compliant software lifecycle toolchain already in place (Jira, Confluence, Polarion) adapted incrementally from the old MDD (C005, C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005","C005-CH3"]},{"text":"Technical file submitted to notified body Zertivo GmbH with 23 written queries returned, 18 of which concern IEC 62304 software lifecycle documentation and traceability between ISO 14971 risk management records and software safety classification (C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005-CH3"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"The notified body has given a six-month window to respond before the file lapses; missing that deadline means restarting the submission, losing a minimum of one full year and delaying entry into two new national markets (C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005-CH3"]},{"text":"The company posted a regulatory affairs manager role three months ago without finding a suitable candidate (C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005-CH3"]},{"text":"The KL-Patch 14 certification process is still underway and cannot proceed while KL-Patch 72 queries remain open; this directly affects the company's plans to launch in German and Dutch markets (C005, C005-CH3).","sourceIds":["C005","C005-CH3"]}]}]}

{"needs":[{"challengeId":"C009-CH1","triage":"research","triageReason":"The challenge is to develop or adapt morphological analysis and script-mixing handling methods for Serbian language search that scale without manual maintenance—an open problem in language engineering for under-resourced languages.","restatement":{"text":"LinguaBot's Elasticsearch-based search system in C009-CH1 misses 18% of real support queries from bank customers because Serbian words have multiple morphological forms (e.g., 'kartica', 'karticu', 'karticom') and users mix Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence. The system has an annotated dataset of 85,000 query-response pairs, two in-house linguists for validation, and a modest 8,000 EUR budget. The goal is to reduce the miss rate below 5% with a solution maintainable as clients add new terminology each quarter, testable within six months.","sourceIds":["C009","C009-CH1","C009/blog/2024-05-22","C009/job/2024-04-10"]},"searchTerms":["morphological analysis","lemmatization","script normalization","information retrieval","inflected language","script mixing","query expansion","Serbian NLP"],"assets":[{"text":"Annotated dataset of 85,000 query-response pairs across four bank and two telecom clients.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1","C009/job/2024-04-10"]},{"text":"Two computational linguists on staff focused on Serbian morphology and dialect variation.","sourceIds":["C009","C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Measured baseline: 18% of 12,000 real support queries return no useful result; more than half of misses traced to morphological mismatch or script confusion.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Existing Elasticsearch search system with basic Croatian stemmer and partial script-normalisation step already deployed.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Custom spaCy pipeline with Serbian morphological components already in production.","sourceIds":["C009"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Budget for tooling or data work is modest—around 8,000 EUR.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Solution must be testable within six months.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Clients add new product terminology every quarter, so the solution must scale maintenance without full re-indexing.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]},{"text":"Target is to get the miss rate below 5% and keep it there with a manageable maintenance process.","sourceIds":["C009-CH1"]}]},{"challengeId":"C009-CH2","triage":"research","triageReason":"The challenge is to determine what multilingual speech model fine-tuning on Serbian telephony audio can achieve and design the data collection and modelling approach—an open problem requiring evaluation under constrained conditions.","restatement":{"text":"LinguaBot's clients require a voice channel by early 2027 (C009-CH2), but commercial automatic speech recognition (ASR) APIs achieve word-error rates above 38% on 300 real call samples from Serbian call-centre audio with background noise, regional accents, and telephony codec artifacts. The company has a corpus of 1,200 anonymised and consented call recordings covering multiple speakers and accents, four ML engineers with limited speech model training experience, and a firm contract deadline in early 2027. The need is to assess whether fine-tuning an existing multilingual model on the 1,200 recordings can reduce word-error rate enough to justify larger data collection, design what additional data would be needed, and deliver a proof-of-concept.","sourceIds":["C009","C009-CH2","C009/job/2024-06-03"]},"searchTerms":["automatic speech recognition","fine-tuning multilingual models","word-error rate","telephony audio","low-resource speech","Serbian speech","acoustic model adaptation","language model fine-tuning"],"assets":[{"text":"Corpus of 1,200 anonymised and consented call recordings from one client covering speaker ages and regional accents.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]},{"text":"Four ML engineers on staff who can integrate ASR output into the existing chat understanding stack.","sourceIds":["C009","C009-CH2"]},{"text":"Measured baseline: word-error rates above 38% on two widely used commercial ASR APIs tested on 300-call sample.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]},{"text":"Existing intent detection and downstream understanding pipeline that would consume ASR transcripts.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Contract renewal in early 2027 with one telecom client requires voice-channel delivery; three bank clients have requested voice by end of 2027.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]},{"text":"Timeline is firm because of the contract.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]},{"text":"The company does not have deep in-house experience in speech model training specifically.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]},{"text":"The focus is on proof-of-concept to show whether fine-tuning an existing multilingual model moves the needle enough to justify larger data-collection effort, not a production-ready system.","sourceIds":["C009-CH2"]}]}]}

{"needs":[{"challengeId":"C012-CH1","triage":"engineering-service","triageReason":"A pipeline for automated reconnaissance and vulnerability enumeration is a known integration problem; the company needs tooling built, not a research breakthrough.","restatement":{"text":"Sentinel Byte's penetration test workflow takes about two weeks per engagement, with four days spent on reconnaissance and vulnerability enumeration; clients are requesting continuous testing and retesting after patches, but the company cannot sustain this at current billing rates without automation (C012-CH1). The company has written fragile Bash scripts that save about two hours per engagement, but needs a reliable pipeline that runs scheduled reconnaissance and vulnerability enumeration, detects changes since the last scan, and delivers structured results to manual testers (C012-CH1). If the initial phase could be reduced from four days to one, the company could offer retest work without adding staff (C012-CH1).","sourceIds":["C012-CH1","C012/blog/2024-04-02"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Nikola Kovačević can dedicate roughly two days per week to a collaborative development project, primarily on tooling and automation topics.","sourceIds":["C012"]},{"text":"The company uses Nmap and Nessus for network scanning, Bash and Python scripts for reconnaissance automation, and Git for version-controlled test documentation.","sourceIds":["C012"]},{"text":"Budget for tooling or a development collaboration is limited—roughly 3,000 to 5,000 euros—but the company is open to a research arrangement where the output is a working prototype.","sourceIds":["C012-CH1"]},{"text":"Multiple real clients are asking for continuous or frequent retesting, including two municipalities and a regional medical supply company.","sourceIds":["C012-CH1"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Budget for tooling is limited to roughly 3,000 to 5,000 euros.","sourceIds":["C012-CH1"]},{"text":"The company plans to move at least part of its reconnaissance workflow onto an automated platform so it can offer continuous monitoring as a service over the next twelve months.","sourceIds":["C012"]},{"text":"Existing Bash scripts break when tool versions change, particularly Nessus, which has changed its output format twice since the scripts were written.","sourceIds":["C012/blog/2024-04-02"]},{"text":"The pipeline must detect changes between scans; the company has attempted a diff step that mostly works but requires manual review to manage noise from edge cases.","sourceIds":["C012/blog/2024-04-02"]}]},{"challengeId":"C012-CH2","triage":"engineering-service","triageReason":"Designing and testing a training curriculum is a known educational design and measurement problem; a student project or instructional design consultant may fit better than a research group.","restatement":{"text":"After audits for two municipalities, Opština Kanjiza and one other, Sentinel Byte's findings went unaddressed because the IT staff could not understand the remediation steps (C012-CH2). Informal afternoon explanation sessions proved effective—one municipality patched four of seven critical issues within a month—but the company currently delivers training informally and without charge (C012-CH2). The company wants to build a structured programme of four to six modules that can be sold alongside audits, but does not know how to design curriculum properly, test knowledge retention, or keep material updated as threats change (C012-CH2).","sourceIds":["C012-CH2","C012/news/2023-11-08"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"The company has technical content in-house about patch management, password policy, phishing recognition, and basic network hygiene, drawn from its audit experience.","sourceIds":["C012-CH2"]},{"text":"The company has evidence that informal training sessions work; one municipality patched four of seven critical issues within a month after an explanation session.","sourceIds":["C012-CH2","C012/news/2023-11-08"]},{"text":"The company has multiple municipal and small business clients who could pilot the training programme.","sourceIds":["C012"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"A good outcome would be a pilot programme ready to test with one municipality client by the end of 2024.","sourceIds":["C012-CH2"]},{"text":"The company plans to formalise its training offering into a repeatable, priced product over the next twelve months.","sourceIds":["C012"]}]},{"challengeId":"C012-CH3","triage":"not-research","triageReason":"This is a regulatory compliance and administrative documentation problem; research cannot solve it.","restatement":{"text":"Sentinel Byte applied to the Serbian Ministry five months ago to register as a certified auditor under the Serbian Information Security Law; the application has been returned three times citing formal deficiencies in document formatting, reference numbering, and professional experience documentation (C012-CH3). The company has consulted a local business lawyer who lacks expertise in this specific regulatory area and needs concrete guidance on what is wrong with the application package (C012-CH3). The company wants the application resolved within three months to be eligible for a municipal procurement round opening in autumn (C012-CH3).","sourceIds":["C012-CH3"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[],"constraints":[{"text":"The company wants to resolve the certification within three months because a municipal procurement round opens in autumn.","sourceIds":["C012-CH3"]},{"text":"Certification would allow the company to bid on public procurement contracts, which it currently cannot do.","sourceIds":["C012-CH3"]}]}]}

{"needs":[{"challengeId":"C018-CH1","triage":"engineering-service","triageReason":"A code generator or scripting tool that maps a known input format (System Extract) to a known output format (ARXML) using a known API (DaVinci Configurator API) can be built and integrated as a standard automation task.","restatement":{"text":"DriveLogic manually generates approximately 3,200 AUTOSAR software component configuration files per project in three weeks using two senior engineers; the company needs to reduce this to under one working day by automating the mapping logic from System Extract to ARXML configuration files using the DaVinci API. (C018-CH1)","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]},"searchTerms":["code generation","AUTOSAR configuration","API automation","template-based synthesis","XML transformation"],"assets":[{"text":"DaVinci Configurator API documentation and two engineers with Python scripting capability.","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]},{"text":"Twenty-seven engineers in-house in Novi Sad, all based in one location.","sourceIds":["C018"]},{"text":"Current project baseline of approximately 3,200 ARXML files per project; experience with two recent projects of this scale.","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"The company loses price-sensitive bids to competitors who have achieved the same work in four days.","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]},{"text":"Output must be a reviewable first-draft configuration set; engineers will still perform review and exception handling.","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]},{"text":"The input is a customer-provided System Extract; the mapping logic between System Extract and final ARXML must be automated.","sourceIds":["C018-CH1"]}]},{"challengeId":"C018-CH2","triage":"research","triageReason":"Systematic generation of test cases that target interface contracts and component interaction faults is an open problem in the absence of an established method; this requires research into specification analysis and test synthesis.","restatement":{"text":"DriveLogic achieves 87–89% branch coverage on software component tests but consistently encounters integration faults at component boundaries in post-delivery customer testing, specifically in the CAN communication stack where SWCs from different suppliers interact with unexpected behavior despite individual specification compliance. The company needs a method or tool that uses ARXML component descriptions and COM configuration to systematically generate test scenarios targeting interface assumptions and interaction contracts. (C018-CH2)","sourceIds":["C018-CH2","C018/blog/2024-04-18"]},"searchTerms":["interface-based testing","contract verification","boundary testing","test case generation","specification mining","component interaction","assumptions analysis"],"assets":[{"text":"Full access to ARXML descriptions of all components, COM configuration, and CANoe environment.","sourceIds":["C018-CH2"]},{"text":"Real project data from four delivered projects showing four CAN communication faults, each occurring at a component boundary between SWCs from different suppliers.","sourceIds":["C018-CH2","C018/blog/2024-04-18"]},{"text":"Coverage measurement infrastructure using LDRA Testbed for branch and MC/DC coverage reporting.","sourceIds":["C018"]},{"text":"CANoe-based network simulation and testing capability for validation.","sourceIds":["C018"]},{"text":"One senior engineer available part-time (40% per week) for collaborative development directly tied to active project tools and methods.","sourceIds":["C018"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Budget in the first phase is not fixed but would not exceed €40,000.","sourceIds":["C018-CH2"]},{"text":"The method must be applicable within the AUTOSAR Classic toolchain and DaVinci Configurator environment currently used on active projects.","sourceIds":["C018"]},{"text":"Current branch coverage threshold is 85% MC/DC for safety-relevant modules; the interface testing problem is orthogonal to this metric.","sourceIds":["C018/website/2024-01-15","C018-CH2"]}]},{"challengeId":"C018-CH3","triage":"not-research","triageReason":"This is a staff training and retention problem; the need is for structured educational content and training delivery, which is a curriculum and instructional design task, not a research question.","restatement":{"text":"Three of five engineers who perform ECU flashing and diagnostic work have no formal training in UDS or OBD-II protocol internals and learned on the job through mentoring. Staff turnover has led to two departures in two years, each replacement requiring €25,000 in internal training cost and three to four months of reduced productivity. The company needs a structured, self-contained training path in UDS and OBD-II internals with practical exercises on simulated ECUs that new hires can complete independently. (C018-CH3)","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},"searchTerms":[],"assets":[{"text":"Five engineers working on ECU flashing and diagnostic tooling; one has formal protocol training.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},{"text":"Internal cheat sheets and informal documentation currently used for on-the-job training.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},{"text":"Experience running one informal workshop but noting it was not systematic.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},{"text":"Active projects with UDS and OBD-II implementation work, providing practical context for training scenarios.","sourceIds":["C018"]}],"constraints":[{"text":"Training must be self-paced and testable for understanding before trainees work on real vehicles.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},{"text":"The problem is retention: senior engineer time is repeatedly consumed on explaining protocol fundamentals to replacements.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]},{"text":"Training must reduce the current three to four months of reduced output during onboarding and eliminate the €25,000 internal training cost per new hire.","sourceIds":["C018-CH3"]}]}]}
